title: Units of the ind-etale lift
statement:
An element of $H_A(\overline C)$, as constructed in
[def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], is invertible if its image in $\overline C$
is invertible.

proof.text: Write $H=H_A(\overline C)$, with cocone maps $\iota_B:B\to H$ and induced map $\rho:H\to\overline C$, as in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Work on a small skeleton of the indexing category: finite presentations $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ form a set, their maps to the fixed ring $\overline C$ form sets, and every indexing object is isomorphic to one of these presentations. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered] this category is filtered. The algebra colimit is also its ring colimit: any compatible family of ring maps from the stages to a ring $R$ has a common restriction $A\to R$, since any two stages have a common successor; giving $R$ that $A$-algebra structure reduces its universal property to the defining algebra colimit. Now [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] (1) gives, for the element $h\in H$ under consideration, a stage $(B,\beta:B\to\overline C)$ and $b\in B$ with $h=\iota_B(b)$. Thus $\rho(h)=\beta(b)$ is a unit.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: choose a stage representative

proof.text: Form $B_b=B[1/b]$ using [def-weil-ring-localization-away], with $\lambda:B\to B_b$. Every $\beta(b^n)=\beta(b)^n$ is a unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] to the multiplicative subset $\{b^n:n\geq0\}$: it supplies a ring map $\beta_b:B_b\to\overline C$ satisfying $\beta_b(c/b^n)=\beta(c)\beta(b)^{-n}$ and $\beta_b\lambda=\beta$. This is an $A$-algebra map because its restriction along $A\to B\to B_b$ is the given structural map $A\to\overline C$.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: extend the map to the localization; Stacks 00CP

proof.text: The stage $B$ is etale of finite presentation over $A$ by [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] (2) to $s=b$ to see that $B_b$ is etale over $A$, and its clause (1), applied to $B_b$, gives finite presentation over $A$. Therefore $(B_b,\beta_b)$ is an object of $\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ and $\lambda$ is a morphism from $(B,\beta)$ to it, since $\beta_b\lambda=\beta$.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: the localization is another indexing object; Stacks 00U1, 00U2

proof.text: In $B_b$ let $u=1/b$, whose defining fraction relations give $(b/1)u=u(b/1)=1$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Cocone compatibility from [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift] gives $\iota_{B_b}(b/1)=\iota_B(b)=h$. Applying the ring homomorphism $\iota_{B_b}$ to the two product identities yields $h\,\iota_{B_b}(u)=\iota_{B_b}(u)h=1$. Hence $h$ is invertible, as required.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: exhibit the inverse in the colimit
